title: Implement the chain-aware squash landing rule in the gate
summary: Read as: build the gate half of design D69 (docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md §4.2, §5 items 3–5). The `athena.candidate/2` records and the core's writing of them are already in the repo. `landing` in athena-gate should therefore accept a squash that closes several jobs when they form a valid fingerprint chain, and still refuse every broken variant.

defaults_applied.how: Add the design's §5 item 4 tests in landing_tests.rs, jobs.rs and history.rs, starting with a hand-built two-job chain. cargo test and clippy must pass.
The design and its two reviews already exist, so this implements them and does not redesign.
The rule is enforced by the gate itself, and enforcement.md rows are updated to name the tests.
The missing detail was recovered from D69 and the design doc.
Limit the change to the gate crate, its tests and the docs that describe it.
Refusal messages and docs are written for an outside reader.

assumptions: 'The gate rule' means the check in crates/athena-gate (invariant.rs landing, jobs.rs, history.rs), not the records or core work. Grep found athena.candidate/2, base_fingerprint and previous_job already in athena-data and athena-core.

The design in docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md §4.2 and §4.3 is followed as written, including its refusal messages and the refusal of chains on multi-parent commits and chains that touch .gitattributes.
Single-job landings stay byte-for-byte as strict as today.
No [history] exempt entry is added or removed, and no governance files change.
Doc updates (enforcement.md rows, D69 status, v0 §7.3 wording, CHANGELOG) are included as the design's §5 item 5 says.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. A hand-built squash that adds the records of two or more jobs linked by previous_job and base_fingerprint, with the last job's fingerprint equal to the squashed tree, passes both invariant::check and jobs::check.

Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. Tests show each of these is refused with the message in design §4.3: a /1 candidate in a chain, no head or a wrong head base, a fork, an unlinked or missing middle job, a broken fingerprint link, a last job that does not match the tree, a chain that changes a .gitattributes file.

Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. A chain on a commit with two parents is refused. A partly landed chain is judged correctly: one job left uses the single-job rule, and two or more left with a landed predecessor, including a /1 predecessor, are accepted.
Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. Chains with repeated fingerprints (a job that reverts an earlier one, a job that changes no governed content) land.

Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. Each per-job check (reading, a prediction written after the work, verdict, candidate commits, verifier invocation, usage, outcome choice, earlier landing) refuses the commit when it fails on a middle job. After a chain lands, repeating one of its jobs is refused by the history walk.
Run `cargo test -p athena-gate`. A single-job squash and every existing landing test behave as before, and `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
The gate's `landing_job` returns the set of jobs, `jobs::check` accepts every job of a chain, and the history state records every job of a chain.

docs/enforcement.md no longer says that squashing a chain is refused and names the new tests. D69 is marked accepted or changed, design §7.3 and the CHANGELOG are updated, and no governance file or records/ path is touched.

out_of_scope: Changing athena-data schemas or athena-core's derivation of previous_job; these already exist.
Passing landing's refusal reason through the merge-commit path in check.
Adding [history] exempt entries or changing athena.toml, workflows or other governance files.
Stopping squash-merging of pull requests (option c of D66).
Signing records or defending against forged records.
departures: The reference forecast comes from mostly small jobs. This one is a large gate change with many tests and a detailed design, so cost and time are higher and the pass probability is lower. I also read the request as only the gate half of D69, which is less certain than the reference acceptance rate assumes.
